mainTopic: Offerings of גוים (קדשי גוים): which קרבן laws apply to them and the sources that exclude them
overview: The amud opens at the end of an argument. רבא asks why anyone would give a practical ruling (הלכה) on a קרבן law that only applies in the days of משיח. אביי answers that we learn all of קדשים for the reward of learning (דרוש וקבל שכר), and רבא clarifies that he only objected to calling it a practical ruling. Then a new משנה teaches that offerings of גוים carry no liability for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא. On slaughtering them outside the עזרה, רבי שמעון exempts and רבי יוסי holds the person liable. A ברייתא adds more rules: no benefit is allowed, but there is no מעילה; there is no תמורה; and a גוי cannot bring נסכים alone, though his animal offerings still need נסכים. רבי יוסי would be strict in all these cases. The גמרא then finds a פסוק-based source for each rule, often a word 'בני ישראל' that leaves out גוים. Along the way it deals with a problem about chaining two היקשים, and it explains why gifts to בדק הבית, which have only קדושת דמים, still carry מעילה. The amud ends as a new ברייתא about impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח begins.

steps.title: Why give a practical ruling for the days of משיח?
steps.stepSummary: The questioner objects to a practical ruling (הלכה) given about a קרבן law, since it can only apply when the בית המקדש is rebuilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we deciding the law for the days of משיח?!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone has just ruled 'the הלכה follows so-and-so' on a קרבן law, and the questioner protests that such a ruling has no use today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laws of קרבנות cannot be practiced without the בית המקדש. So the challenge is: what is the point of a practical ruling that nobody can act on until משיח comes?

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law, the final ruling
For the days of משיח, when the בית המקדש will be rebuilt

phrases.english: A practical ruling for the days of the Messiah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא לִמְשִׁיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practical ruling given just before this section begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The issuing of a practical הלכה about a קרבן law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling is meant to guide action, and קרבנות cannot be offered today, so the ruling seems useless.

steps.title: אביי: then all of זבחים would be pointless, but we learn for reward
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if this were a problem, the whole topic of slaughtering קדשים should not be taught. We learn it anyway for the reward of learning, and the same applies here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, the whole topic of slaughtering sacrifices should not be taught, since it is all law for the days of משיח! Rather, we follow the rule 'learn and receive reward.' Here too, learn and receive reward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the objection by showing it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being useful only in the days of משיח were a reason not to deal with a law, we could not learn any of מסכת זבחים. Since we clearly do learn it, because learning תורה earns reward by itself, there is nothing wrong with dealing with this law too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so...' — opens an argument that the other position leads to an unacceptable result
Slaughtering sacrifices, the whole topic of מסכת זבחים
Learn and receive reward: learning תורה is rewarded even when it has no practical use now

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that learning laws we cannot practice today, like קדשים, is a full מצוה of תלמוד תורה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so,
let the whole topic of slaughtering sacrifices not be taught,
since it is law for the days of the Messiah!
Rather, we say: learn and receive reward;
here too, learn and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 1 by showing it would rule out all of קדשים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole objection that laws for the days of משיח are not worth dealing with
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection proves too much: it would also cancel learning all of שחיטת קדשים, which we obviously do learn for reward.

steps.title: The questioner clarifies: learning is fine, a 'ruling' is not needed
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains that he never objected to learning these laws, only to deciding a practical ruling on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I am saying to you: why do I need a practical ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner answers אביי by narrowing what his objection really was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that we learn קדשים for reward. His point is different: learning and discussing is one thing, but announcing 'the הלכה is like this' only makes sense for something people can act on now.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am telling you — the speaker clarifies what he meant
Why do I need it? What is it for?

phrases.english: This is what I am saying to you:
Why do I need a practical ruling?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's rejection by explaining that the original objection was only about a practical ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the original objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי understood the objection as against dealing with these laws at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The objection was only against issuing a practical ruling, not against learning.

steps.title: Another version of the same answer
steps.stepSummary: A second version puts the questioner's answer in different words: 'I was talking about the ruling.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: he said to him: I was speaking about the ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second wording of the same reply from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meaning does not change. Either way, the questioner says his surprise was about the words 'the הלכה is,' not about learning the topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of how the conversation was reported
I was speaking about the practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees we learn קדשים for the reward of learning (דרוש וקבל שכר). The only question raised was whether it makes sense to announce a practical ruling on it.

phrases.english: Another version: he said to him:
I was speaking about the practical ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same answer as step 3 in a different wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the objection was against learning these laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: The objection was only about calling it a practical הלכה.

steps.title: The משנה: offerings of גוים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that eating offerings of גוים carries no liability for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא. רבי שמעון exempts one who slaughters them outside the עזרה, and רבי יוסי holds him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Offerings of גוים — one is not liable for them for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא. And one who slaughters them outside is exempt. These are the words of רבי שמעון. רבי יוסי holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching how offerings brought by non-Jews differ from Jewish offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are real offerings, but some punishments that apply to Jewish קרבנות do not apply to them: פיגול, נותר, and eating while טמא. On slaughtering them outside the עזרה (שחוטי חוץ) there is a מחלוקת: רבי שמעון exempts, and רבי יוסי holds the person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
Offerings set aside as holy by non-Jews
An offering ruined by the intent to eat it after its allowed time
Meat of an offering left over past its allowed time
One who slaughters them outside the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say these offerings are not holy. They are still קדשים; the משנה only says certain specific punishments do not apply to them.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Offerings consecrated by gentiles —
one is not liable for them due to piggul,
leftover meat, or eating while impure;
and one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
Rabbi Yosei holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי גוֹיִם – אֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings of גוים carry no liability for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא. Slaughtering them outside: רבי שמעון exempts, רבי יוסי holds liable.

steps.title: ברייתא: no benefit allowed, but no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that one may not benefit from offerings of גוים, but there is no מעילה if one does. It repeats that there is no liability for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: Offerings of גוים — one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה for them. And one is not liable for them for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a fuller list of the rules of offerings of גוים, starting with benefit and מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using these offerings is forbidden from the start, since they are holy. But the special penalty of מעילה, for misusing holy property, does not apply after the fact. Then the ברייתא repeats the משנה's three exemptions.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא's discussion begins
One may not benefit from them
There is no מעילה (penalty for misusing holy property)

phrases.english: Gemara: The Sages taught:
Offerings consecrated by gentiles —
one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse,
and one is not liable for them due to piggul,
leftover meat, or eating while impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קׇדְשֵׁי גוֹיִם – לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings of גוים: no benefit allowed, no מעילה, and no liability for פיגול, נותר, or eating while טמא.

steps.title: ברייתא continues: no תמורה, no separate נסכים, but their offerings need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that גוים cannot make a תמורה and cannot bring נסכים by themselves, but their animal offerings do need נסכים. This is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they cannot make a תמורה, and they cannot bring נסכים, but their offerings require נסכים. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list and says the whole list is the opinion of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי who tries to swap an animal for a holy one (תמורה) does not make it holy. A גוי also cannot bring נסכים as a separate offering. But when a גוי brings an animal offering, it still needs its usual נסכים alongside it.

keyTerms.meaning: Trying to swap an ordinary animal for a holy one, which normally makes the new animal holy too
Wine (and flour and oil) offerings poured on the מזבח
Requires

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, offerings of גוים are holy, but many of the special laws and punishments of Jewish offerings do not apply to them: מעילה, פיגול, נותר, טמא, שחוטי חוץ, and תמורה. Their animal offerings still need נסכים.

phrases.english: and they cannot make a substitute,
and they cannot bring libations,
phrases.notes: This means נסכים brought by themselves as their own offering, not together with an animal.

phrases.english: but their offerings require libations.
These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין מְבִיאִין נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גוים cannot make a תמורה or bring separate נסכים, but their animal offerings require נסכים (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: רבי יוסי would be strict in all these cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues that all the stringencies should apply to offerings of גוים, because the פסוק says 'לה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: I think we should be strict in all of these cases, because the פסוק says about them 'to ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יוסי disagrees with the lenient rules just listed. He says all the strict laws should apply to offerings of גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous lines said a גוי's offering carries no פיגול, נותר or טמא liability. רבי יוסי reads the word 'לה׳' in the פסוק that includes גוים' offerings as showing these offerings fully belong to ה׳. If they fully belong to ה׳, all the usual laws should apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: I see; I think it makes sense
to be strict
to ה׳; for G-d

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
I see reason to be strict in all of them,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the laws just listed, such as פיגול, נותר and טמא. As the next line and the גמרא show, he still agrees that a גוי's altar offerings carry no מעילה.

phrases.english: as it is stated regarding them: "to the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוסי רואה אני בכולן להחמיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the lenient rulings of the ברייתא quoted in steps 6-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, offerings of גוים are fully holy to ה׳, so all the stringencies apply.

steps.title: The rule applies to altar offerings, not to Temple-maintenance gifts
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי יוסי's statement, the ברייתא limits the 'no מעילה' rule to קדשי מזבח. Items a גוי gives for בדק הבית do carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? To things given for the מזבח. But things given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש do carry מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי's statement in the ברייתא ends by setting a limit. The 'no מעילה' rule covers only offerings for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of holy property: things set aside for the מזבח (קדשי מזבח) and things given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש (קדשי בדק הבית). When a גוי gives to בדק הבית, the ברייתא says regular מעילה liability does apply.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
Items made holy for the מזבח, meaning offerings
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
One is liable for מעילה, meaning misusing holy property

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי's altar offerings carry no מעילה, but his gifts to בדק הבית do.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With items consecrated for the altar,
but with items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
one is liable for misusing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: במה דברים אמורים בקדשי מזבח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by limiting the scope of the 'no מעילה' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'no מעילה' rule covers only a גוי's קדשי מזבח. His קדשי בדק הבית do carry מעילה.

steps.title: The ban on benefit is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the ברייתא. The rule 'one may not benefit' is a rabbinic rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not benefit, and there is no מעילה.' 'One may not benefit' means by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back and explains the ברייתא one line at a time. It starts with the ban on benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line answers a puzzle. How can benefit be forbidden if there is no מעילה? The answer is that the ban is only דרבנן. The תורה law of מעילה does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Getting benefit or use from something
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: "One may not benefit, but there is no liability for misuse."
"One may not benefit": by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא נהנין ולא מועלין לא נהנין מדרבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's line-by-line explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on benefiting from a גוי's offerings is דרבנן.

steps.title: Why there is no מעילה: a link to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: There is no מעילה because מעילה is learned from תרומה through the shared word 'חטא'. תרומה is limited to 'בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is no מעילה' because the תנא learns מעילה from תרומה through the word 'sin' that appears in both. About תרומה the פסוק says 'בני ישראל', which means not גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the תורה source for the rule that there is no מעילה with a גוי's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה links מעילה to תרומה, because the word 'חטא' appears in both. The תרומה laws are limited to 'בני ישראל', so that limit carries over to מעילה. The result is that holy items of גוים are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from
Sin. The shared word that links the two topics
Learning a law from a word that appears in two places
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: "But there is no liability for misuse":
because he derives misuse
from "sin"–"sin" in the case of תרומה,
phrases.notes: The word 'sin' appears in ויקרא 5:15 about מעילה and in ויקרא 22:9 about תרומה.

phrases.english: and regarding תרומה it is written:
"the children of Israel", and not gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא מועלין דגמר מעילה חטא חטא מתרומה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the same line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מעילה with a גוי's offerings, because מעילה is learned from תרומה, which is limited to בני ישראל.

steps.title: Why no liability for פיגול, נותר or טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one is not liable for it because of פיגול, נותר or טמא.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and asks why these three laws do not apply. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a תורה source for leaving גוים' offerings out of each of these three laws. It will build the answer step by step.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Offering meat left over past its time
Eating holy meat while טמא
What is the reason?

phrases.english: "And one is not liable for it
due to פיגול, נותר, or impurity."
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: ואין חייבין עליו משום פיגול נותר וטמא מאי טעמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה source that leaves a גוי's offerings out of פיגול, נותר and טמא liability.

steps.title: פיגול is learned from נותר
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: פיגול is linked to נותר through the shared word 'עון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because פיגול is learned from נותר through the word 'iniquity' that appears in both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by linking פיגול to נותר. The chain continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עון' appears with both פיגול and נותר, so the two laws are linked. Whatever limit applies to נותר will also apply to פיגול. The next part of the גמרא will show where that limit comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Iniquity. The shared word that links פיגול and נותר
It comes from; it is learned from

phrases.english: Because פיגול is derived
from "iniquity"–"iniquity" in the case of נותר,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18 for פיגול and ויקרא 19:8 for נותר. The explanation keeps going in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: דאתי פיגול עון עון מנותר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פיגול is linked to נותר through the shared word 'עון'. The rest of the chain follows next.

steps.title: נותר is learned from טומאה, which excludes גוים
steps.stepSummary: נותר is linked to טומאה through the shared word 'חילול'. The טומאה פסוק says 'בני ישראל', so גוים are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And נותר itself is learned from טומאה through the shared word 'profaning'. In the טומאה פסוק it says 'children of Israel', which means not gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain it began in step 13. פיגול comes from נותר, and now נותר comes from טומאה, where the פסוק mentions 'בני ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בני ישראל' limit is written by טומאה, not by פיגול. Two גזירה שוות carry it over: 'עון' takes it from נותר to פיגול, and 'חילול' takes it from טומאה to נותר. So the rule of פיגול does not apply to a גוי's קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of a קרבן left over past its time limit
Profaning; the shared word linking נותר and טומאה
Ritual impurity; here, eating קדשים while impure
Gentiles

phrases.english: And נותר itself is derived
through 'profaning'–'profaning' from impurity
and regarding impurity it is written: 'the children of Israel'
but not gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָתֵי נוֹתָר ״חִילּוּל״–״חִילּוּל״ מִטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פיגול comes from נותר through 'עון'. נותר comes from טומאה through 'חילול'. The טומאה פסוק says 'בני ישראל', so גוים are excluded.

steps.title: Why can't a gentile make a substitute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that a גוי cannot make a תמורה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And gentiles cannot make a substitute. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule in the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question follows the same pattern as step 12: each rule in the ברייתא needs a source that excludes גוים. The answer will have to find 'בני ישראל' somewhere connected to תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution: trying to swap a קרבן for another animal, which makes both holy
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And they cannot make a substitute.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a גוי's קרבן cannot become a תמורה

steps.title: A chain of two juxtapositions leads to 'children of Israel'
steps.stepSummary: תמורה is linked by a היקש to מעשר בהמה. מעשר בהמה is linked by a היקש to מעשר דגן. By מעשר דגן the פסוק says 'בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because substitution is placed next to animal tithe, and animal tithe is placed next to grain tithe. By grain tithe it is written 'children of Israel', which means not gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by building a chain of two היקשים that ends at a פסוק saying 'בני ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no direct 'בני ישראל' by תמורה, so the גמרא links it in two steps. It goes from תמורה to מעשר בהמה, and then to מעשר דגן. The exclusion of גוים passes back along the chain to תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is juxtaposed; placed together in the פסוק so they share laws
Tithe of animals: every tenth animal is holy
Tithe of grain

phrases.english: Because substitution is juxtaposed to animal tithe,
and animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe,
and regarding grain tithe it is written: 'the children of Israel'
but not gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתַּקַּשׁ תְּמוּרָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמורה is linked to מעשר בהמה, and מעשר בהמה is linked to מעשר דגן. מעשר דגן is limited to 'בני ישראל'.

steps.title: Can a juxtaposition teach through another juxtaposition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the chain. A law learned through a היקש should not be able to go on and teach through a second היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does something learned through a juxtaposition go back and teach through a juxtaposition?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 16. That chain used two היקשים in a row, which is normally not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים there is a rule that a law learned through a היקש cannot pass on to a third case through another היקש. Here מעשר בהמה learned from מעשר דגן by היקש, and then taught תמורה by another היקש. That looks like exactly what the rule forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that was itself learned through a היקש
Goes back and teaches another case

steps.confusionAlert: This limit on chaining היקשים applies to קדשים. That is why the answer in the next step points out that מעשר דגן is not קדשים.

phrases.english: But does a matter learned through a juxtaposition
go back and teach through a juxtaposition?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The chain of two היקשים from step 16
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In קדשים, a law learned through a היקש may not teach through another היקש.

steps.title: Grain tithe is non-sacred, so the limit doesn't apply
steps.stepSummary: מעשר דגן is חולין, so the rule against chaining היקשים does not block this chain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grain tithe is non-sacred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the chain starts from מעשר דגן, which is not קדשים. So the קדשים rule does not stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on chaining היקשים is only for קדשים. The source at the start of the chain, מעשר דגן, is חולין. So the גמרא says the chain is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-sacred, ordinary items
Sacred items, such as קרבנות

phrases.english: Grain tithe is non-sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן חוּלִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chain is forbidden because it uses two היקשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chain is allowed because its source, מעשר דגן, is חולין.

steps.title: But what about the view that follows the case being taught?
steps.stepSummary: The answer of step 18 works for the view that we follow the teaching source. For the view that we follow the case being taught, which here is תמורה (קדשים), the problem returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says we follow the teaching case. But for the one who says we follow the case being taught, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. That answer only fits one opinion about which case decides whether the קדשים rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion says we look at the teaching source (מעשר דגן, which is חולין), so the chain is allowed. The other opinion says we look at the case being taught (תמורה, which is קדשים), so the ban should apply. Step 20 answers this with a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
We follow the case that teaches
We follow the case that is being taught
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
we follow the teaching source;
phrases.notes: He means we look at where the law comes from, here מעשר דגן, which is חולין.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says
we follow the case being taught,
phrases.notes: Here that is תמורה, which is קדשים.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר מְלַמֵּד אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that מעשר דגן is חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the opinion that follows the case being taught, the case is תמורה, which is קדשים, so the ban on chaining היקשים should still apply.

steps.title: A new reason: an obligation with no fixed time is only for Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the chain of היקשים. It explains instead that מעשר בהמה is an obligation with no fixed time, and such obligations are brought only by Jews, not by גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מעשר בהמה is an obligation that has no fixed time. An obligation with no fixed time is brought by Jews, but גוים do not bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge of step 19 knocked out the chain of היקשים, so the גמרא gives a different reason why a גוי has no מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need the second היקש to מעשר דגן. A גוי is left out of מעשר בהמה simply because it is a fixed obligation with no set time, and those belong only to Jews. The first היקש, from תמורה to מעשר בהמה, still stands, so a גוי also cannot make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
An obligatory offering, one a person must bring
A fixed time
They bring

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי cannot make a תמורה because תמורה is tied to מעשר בהמה. מעשר בהמה is an obligation with no fixed time, and only Jews bring that kind of obligation.

phrases.english: Rather, animal tithe is an obligation
that has no fixed time,
and an obligation that has no fixed time —
Jews bring it, gentiles do not bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה חוֹבָה שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by replacing the second היקש with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: a reason based on the type of obligation instead of a second היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי was left out only through the chain תמורה → מעשר בהמה → מעשר דגן ('בני ישראל'), and that chain broke down.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר בהמה is an obligation with no fixed time, which only Jews bring, so the single היקש from תמורה is enough.

steps.title: Source that a גוי cannot bring libations on their own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's next rule, that גוים do not bring נסכים. It cites a ברייתא that learns this from the word 'אזרח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'And they do not bring נסכים.' The רבנן taught: 'אזרח' (homeborn) means a homeborn person brings נסכים, but a גוי does not bring נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and gives its source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about נסכים says 'אזרח', a native Jew. That word limits bringing נסכים as their own offering to Jews, so a גוי cannot bring them alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: wine, flour and oil brought with or apart from an animal offering
Homeborn; a native Jew

phrases.english: "And they do not bring libations."
The Rabbis taught: "Homeborn" —
a homeborn brings libations,
but the gentile does not bring libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְבִיאִין נְסָכִים. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the ברייתא after finishing the topic of תמורה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a גוי cannot bring נסכים on their own

steps.title: A gentile's burnt offering still needs libations
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe a גוי's עולה should not need נסכים at all. The word 'ככה' teaches that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think his עולה does not need נסכים. So the פסוק says 'ככה' (so), teaching that every offering needs נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks a wrong conclusion someone might draw from the word 'אזרח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אזרח' only stops a גוי from bringing נסכים as their own separate offering. 'ככה' shows that the normal נסכים that go with an animal offering still apply to a גוי's עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a possible mistake)
The פסוק teaches
Burnt offering
Requires

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different kinds of נסכים here. A גוי cannot bring נסכים as their own offering, but his animal עולה still needs its regular נסכים.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא עוֹלָתוֹ טְעוּנָה נְסָכִים?
phrases.english: One might think his burnt offering should not require libations?
The verse says: "So."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:11: 'So shall it be done' for each animal, so every animal offering gets נסכים.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא עוֹלָתוֹ טְעוּנָה נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the lesson of 'אזרח' from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ככה' teaches that a גוי's עולה still requires the regular accompanying נסכים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's limit, and what his reason is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the ברייתא. He is strict in all these cases, and he limits the gentile exemption to items set aside for the altar. The גמרא then asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: I see that in all of them we should be strict. When is this said? With items set aside for the מזבח, and so on. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's ruling and then asks why he splits items for the מזבח from items for בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'כו׳' (etc.) means the rest of the line is known: things a גוי gave to בדק הבית do carry מעילה. The question is why the two kinds of holy items should be treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict
In what case are these words said? (limits a rule)
Items set aside for the altar
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
I see in all of them to be stringent.
In what case are these words said?
In items consecrated for the altar, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the line: items a גוי gave for בדק הבית do carry מעילה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי רוֹאֶה אֲנִי בְּכוּלָּן לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from נסכים to the next part of the ברייתא, רבי יוסי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי treats items for the מזבח differently from items for בדק הבית

steps.title: מעילה is learned from תרומה, so only body-holy items are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that מעילה is learned from תרומה through the word 'חטא'. So the gentile exemption covers only items with קדושת הגוף like תרומה, and not בדק הבית items, which have only קדושת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: since מעילה is learned from תרומה through the word 'חטא' in both places, it is like תרומה, which is holy in its body. But items for בדק הבית have only money-value holiness, so the exemption does not cover them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 23 and explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה ties מעילה to תרומה. That link only works for items that are like תרומה, meaning holy in their very body. Items for בדק הבית are holy only for their money value, so the comparison does not reach them, and a גוי's gift to בדק הבית still carries מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
Misusing holy property
The word 'sin' in both places, linking them (a גזירה שוה)
Holiness of the item itself
Holiness of the item's money value only
Upkeep of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Because מעילה is learned from תרומה, the exemption for a גוי's items covers only קדשי מזבח, which are holy in their body (קדושת הגוף) like תרומה. His gifts to בדק הבית are holy only for their value (קדושת דמים), so they do carry מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The split between קדושת הגוף and קדושת דמים comes up again and again in קדשים. Here it decides how far a comparison learned from תרומה can reach.

phrases.english: He holds: when misuse is learned
"sin"–"sin" from teruma,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:15 (מעילה) and ויקרא 22:9 (תרומה) both use the word 'חטא'.

phrases.english: it is similar to teruma,
which is sacred with inherent sanctity;
but the sanctity of Temple maintenance,
which is sanctity of value — no.
phrases.notes: He means the gentile exemption does not cover these items, so מעילה applies to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר כִּי גָּמְרָה מְעִילָה חֵט חֵט מִתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעילה is learned from תרומה, so the exemption covers only items with קדושת הגוף like תרומה (קדשי מזבח), not בדק הבית items, which have קדושת דמים.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: impure blood sprinkled by mistake is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If blood became impure and a כהן sprinkled it on the מזבח by mistake, the offering is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if blood became impure and the כהן sprinkled it on the altar, and he did this by mistake, the offering is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about blood that became impure before it was sprinkled. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will use this ברייתא to keep analyzing רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that became טמא should not be put on the מזבח. Still, this ברייתא says that if the כהן did it בשוגג, by mistake, the offering works after the fact. The ברייתא is only starting here, and the following lines will add more cases to compare.

keyTerms.meaning: Became ritually impure
He sprinkled it on the altar
By mistake, without knowing
It was accepted; the offering works

steps.confusionAlert: 'Accepted' here only means the offering counts after it already happened. It does not mean a כהן may sprinkle impure blood to begin with.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Blood that became impure, and he sprinkled it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן, and he sprinkled the blood on the מזבח.

phrases.english: if by mistake, it is accepted,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי יוסי's reason in Step 24, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא to keep examining his view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח by mistake still makes the offering accepted after the fact.
